title: Episode 225: CppNorth & Flux Plans, The Slow Death of Twitter and More!

sentences.en: Phil told me once, Phil Nash, who organizes a bunch of conferences, he told me, I think he said that, like,
sentences.zh: 菲尔曾告诉我，菲尔·纳什，他组织过很多会议，他告诉我，我想他是这么说的，

sentences.en: they get 80% of their submissions in the last 24 hours before they're closing.
sentences.zh: 他们80%的投稿都是在截止前最后24小时内收到的。

sentences.en: So, I am definitely one of those people.
sentences.zh: 所以，我绝对是那种人。

sentences.en: Leave it to the last minute.
sentences.zh: 拖到最后一分钟。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 225, recorded on February 17th, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到 ADSP 播客，第 225 期，录制于 2025 年 2 月 17 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Ben, we conclude our conversation with Tristan Brindle.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天我的联合主持人是本，我们将结束与特里斯坦·布林德尔的对话。

sentences.en: In this episode, we talk about plans for CPP North 2025, plans for Flux, the slow death of Twitter, and more.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们讨论了 2025 年加拿大 C++ 北方大会的计划、Flux 的计划、推特的缓慢消亡等等。

sentences.en: Well, I was going to, I mean, I don't know if you were going to wrap that up, Connor, but I had, I was going to ask Tristan, are you, are you playing,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我本来打算，我是说，我不知道你是不是要总结一下，康纳，但我有，我本来想问特里斯坦，你，你有没有在玩，

sentences.en: will we see you in Toronto this year?
sentences.zh: 今年我们在多伦多能见到你吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，会，绝对的。

sentences.en: Well, all being well, I mean, I'm going to, if I get accepted for the CPP North, I'd certainly like to go again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一切顺利的话，我是说，如果我被加拿大 C++ 北方大会接受了，我当然很想再去一次。

sentences.en: I've, what is it, it's, this will be the fourth one, right?
sentences.zh: 我已经，怎么说呢，这将是第四届了，对吧？

sentences.en: This is the fourth, yes.
sentences.zh: 这是第四届，是的。

sentences.en: Two of them were at the King Edward Hotel, and I believe this one.
sentences.zh: 其中两届在爱德华国王酒店举行，我想这一届也是。

sentences.en: Last year was at Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 去年是在微软举行的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's at Microsoft again, July 20th to 23rd, and Call for Papers is open.
sentences.zh: 对，我想今年还是在微软，7 月 20 日到 23 日，论文征集已经开始了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I know it closes.
sentences.zh: 我知道它快截止了。

sentences.en: Today we're recording on February 17th, which is a holiday in Canada.
sentences.zh: 今天我们是在 2 月 17 日录音，这是加拿大的一个节日。

sentences.en: Well, this part of our recording won't maybe come out next week, but part of our recording will.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们录音的这部分可能不会在下周播出，但部分内容会的。

sentences.en: Important dates, right at the top.
sentences.zh: 重要日期，就在最显眼的地方。

sentences.en: It says Call for Speakers closes on the 23rd, which is six days from now, which means by the time you're listening to it, the CFP is closed.
sentences.zh: 上面说演讲者征集在 23 日截止，也就是从现在算起六天后，这意味着当你听到这期节目时，CFP 已经截止了。

sentences.en: However, if it gets extended by a month, which sometimes it does get extended.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果它延期一个月的话，有时候确实会延期。

sentences.en: I did see that C++ Now's CFP window got extended.
sentences.zh: 我确实看到 C++ Now 的 CFP 期限延长了。

sentences.en: Well, it got extended because of the committee meeting, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，延长是因为委员会会议，我想。

sentences.en: That was the reason they gave, you know, we're extending it to allow the folks who were at the committee meeting to have time to submit afterwards.
sentences.zh: 他们给出的理由是，你知道，我们延长它，是为了让参加委员会会议的人有时间在会后提交。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, I mean, odds are, listeners, if you were thinking of submitting, CFP is closed.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，听众朋友们，如果你当时在考虑投稿，现在 CFP 已经结束了。

sentences.en: I'll say now that maybe there was a possibility that future me, according to today, but past me, according to when you're hearing this, had the energy to insert a CFP closes soon.
sentences.zh: 我现在要说的是，也许未来的我（站在今天来看，但在你听到时已经是过去的我）有精力插播一句“CFP 即将截止”。

sentences.en: But these days, whenever I say if I have the energy, I rarely do.
sentences.zh: 但现在，每当我提到“如果我有精力”时，我往往都没有。

sentences.en: Or it's not even that I rarely do.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至不是我很少有精力。

sentences.en: It's that I don't hear myself reminding me to go and do it.
sentences.zh: 而是我根本没听到自己在提醒自己去做这件事。

sentences.en: So by the time I'm editing in this, I've forgotten that I need to add it.
sentences.zh: 所以当我剪辑到这里时，我已经忘了我需要把它加进去。

sentences.en: And then it's a month later and I was like, oh, yeah, I said I might do that.
sentences.zh: 然后过了一个月，我就想，哦，对哦，我说过我可能会这么做的。

sentences.en: And then I've forgotten.
sentences.zh: 然后我又给忘了。

sentences.en: Have you submitted a talk to CFP North?
sentences.zh: 你给加拿大 C++ 北方大会投过稿吗？

sentences.en: I have not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: I am still thinking.
sentences.zh: 我还在考虑。

sentences.en: I've got a couple different ideas and there's a chance, too, I might be going to a couple conferences.
sentences.zh: 我有几个不同的想法，而且我也有可能会去参加几个会议。

sentences.en: This is in Australia, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实这是在澳大利亚的。

sentences.en: Oh, crikey.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And they've got a series of conferences in, I believe, the three cities are Adelaide, Brisbane, and actually, I should get this right before.
sentences.zh: 他们有一系列会议，我相信这三个城市是阿德莱德、布里斯班，其实，我应该在之前就把这个搞清楚。

sentences.en: Although it might not even be on their website right now.
sentences.zh: 尽管它现在甚至可能不在他们的网站上。

sentences.en: What are the conferences?
sentences.zh: 这是些什么会议？

sentences.en: The series conferences, they're called YOW.
sentences.zh: 这一系列会议叫做 YOW。

sentences.en: Oh, I know them.
sentences.zh: 哦，我知道。

sentences.en: Which is, yeah, I've seen a ton of their talks.
sentences.zh: 那就是，是的，我看过他们的大量演讲。

sentences.en: In fact, one of my favorite talks of all time is by an individual.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我最喜欢的有史以来的演讲之一就是由一个人做的。

sentences.en: Oh, am I going to forget his name?
sentences.zh: 哦，我不会把他的名字给忘了吧？

sentences.en: There's actually two of them and people confuse them all the time.
sentences.zh: 其实有两个这样的人，人们总是把他们搞混。

sentences.en: I can just go to my list of every single talk I've ever watched, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我可以直接打开我看过的所有演讲的列表。

sentences.en: And it was, the title of it is Vectors in the title.
sentences.zh: 那是，标题里带有“向量（Vectors）”这个词。

sentences.en: Yes, by Dave Thomas.
sentences.zh: 是的，由戴夫·托马斯主讲。

sentences.en: There's two Dave Thomases.
sentences.zh: 有两个戴夫·托马斯。

sentences.en: And this is only one of them.
sentences.zh: 而这只是其中之一。

sentences.en: That's the Dave Thomas who wrote Ruby on Rails?
sentences.zh: 那是写了《Ruby on Rails》的那个戴夫·托马斯吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Am I getting that right?
sentences.zh: 我没记错吧？

sentences.en: That might have been.
sentences.zh: 可能吧。

sentences.en: Or is it something else?
sentences.zh: 还是别的什么人？

sentences.en: But this Dave Thomas was heavily involved, I think, with organizing the go-to conferences.
sentences.zh: 但这个戴夫·托马斯深度参与了，我认为，组织 GoTo 会议的工作。

sentences.en: And YOW was like a sibling or under the same umbrella.
sentences.zh: 而 YOW 就像是它的兄弟会议，或者属于同一个伞形项目。

sentences.en: And there's a talk that he gave back in 2014 called Living in Big Data with Vector Functional Programming.
sentences.zh: 他在 2014 年做过一个演讲，叫做《用向量函数式编程生活在大数据中》。

sentences.en: And it was one of the talks that I watched back in December of 2019 that, like, was me at the edge of the Alice in Wonderland rabbit hole that is APL and array languages.
sentences.zh: 这是我在 2019 年 12 月看过的演讲之一，它让我站在了 APL 和数组语言这个“爱丽丝梦游仙境”般兔子洞的边缘。

sentences.en: And it's not online anymore, though.
sentences.zh: 不过它现在不在线上了。

sentences.en: It got moved.
sentences.zh: 它被移走了。

sentences.en: And it actually might be on the Internet Archive.
sentences.zh: 其实它可能在互联网档案馆（Internet Archive）上。

sentences.en: I always forget to check the Internet Archive.
sentences.zh: 我总是忘记去检查互联网档案馆。

sentences.en: Anyways, the point being is they're asking me about topics right now.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，重点是他们现在正在向我征求话题。

sentences.en: So I've been trying to think.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在思考。

sentences.en: I will definitely be submitting a talk.
sentences.zh: 我一定会投一篇演讲的。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, I have a bunch of talk topics.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我是说，我有很多演讲话题。

sentences.en: But these days, a lot of them are more functional programming, less C++-y.
sentences.zh: 但如今，其中很多都更偏向函数式编程，而 C++ 的味道没那么浓。

sentences.en: Well, CPP North is looking for general, has in previous years, been looking for general programming talks as not just C++-specific things, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，加拿大 C++ 北方大会一直在寻找通用的，在往届中，一直都在寻找通用的编程演讲，而不仅仅是 C++ 的专项内容，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I wrote the first CFP, but I've got to be honest, I actually haven't read it since I wasn't program chair.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我写了第一份 CFP，但我得老实说，自从我不再担任程序委员会主席之后，我其实就没再读过它了。

sentences.en: So my guess is it has changed.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜它已经变了。

sentences.en: I haven't submitted yet, although I have been, especially in the last few days, I have been waking up at, like, 5 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我还没投稿，尽管我一直在，尤其是在过去几天里，我经常在早上 5 点左右醒来，

sentences.en: full of thoughts and having to note them down by the side of the bed.
sentences.zh: 满脑子都是想法，不得不把它们记在床头。

sentences.en: Any preview thoughts?
sentences.zh: 有什么提前透露的想法吗？

sentences.en: And I will ask Tristan as well, because it sounds like you already submitted, so...
sentences.zh: 我也要问问特里斯坦，因为听起来你好像已经投过稿了，所以……

sentences.en: Me?
sentences.zh: 我？

sentences.en: No, I have not yet.
sentences.zh: 没有，我还没有。

sentences.en: So none of us have submitted.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谁都没投。

sentences.en: Yes, and I shouldn't prejudice the program committee process.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我不应该对程序委员会的评审流程产生先入为主的影响。

sentences.en: Phil told me once, Phil Nash, who organizes a bunch of conferences, he told me, I think he said that, like,
sentences.zh: 菲尔曾告诉我，菲尔·纳什，他组织过很多会议，他告诉我，我想他是这么说的，

sentences.en: they get 80% of their submissions in the last 24 hours before they're closing.
sentences.zh: 他们 80% 的投稿都是在截止前最后 24 小时内收到的。

sentences.en: Yeah, wow.
sentences.zh: 哇，真是这样。

sentences.en: So I am definitely one of those people.
sentences.zh: 所以我绝对是那种人。

sentences.en: Leave it to the last minute.
sentences.zh: 拖到最后一分钟。

sentences.en: I usually put on my calendar one day, one calendar day before the actual deadline that says this is the deadline.
sentences.zh: 我通常会在日历上把实际截止日期前的一天标为“这就是截止日期”。

sentences.en: And then, so usually I'm actually 24 hours in advance, but that's only because I lie to myself about when the deadline is.
sentences.zh: 然后，通常我其实会提前 24 小时完成，但这只是因为我对截止日期撒了谎。

sentences.en: Otherwise, there's a chance I'll end up missing.
sentences.zh: 否则，我很有可能会错过。

sentences.en: But yes, we might all be in the same spot.
sentences.zh: 但没错，我们可能都处在同样的境地。

sentences.en: The question I was going to circle back to was you mentioned, and it might have to do with this GitHub PR that I came across from 2023, about future design plans for Flux.
sentences.zh: 我要转回来的问题是，你提到了——这可能与我偶然看到的 2023 年的一个 GitHub PR 有关——关于 Flux 未来的设计规划。

sentences.en: And the PR title is Expanding the Internal Iteration API, which I'm not sure if that's the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而这个 PR 的标题是《扩展内部迭代 API》，我不太确定这是否是同一回事。

sentences.en: But you mentioned that you have potential future design plans.
sentences.zh: 但你提到你对未来有潜在的设计规划。

sentences.en: So anyways, if you want to share with us and the listeners what those are, if it's of interest, I'd be curious.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，如果你想和我们及听众分享这些内容，如果大家感兴趣的话，我会很好奇。

sentences.en: Way to start.
sentences.zh: 好一个开场。

sentences.en: So it is that PR, or I think it's an issue that was open, it kind of morphed into what I'm thinking about now, because Flux is kind of, strangely for a library called Flux,
sentences.zh: 所以确实是那个 PR，或者我想那是一个曾经开启的 Issue，它慢慢演变成了我现在的想法，因为 Flux 有点像——对于一个叫做 Flux 的库来说有些奇怪——

sentences.en: it's kind of stable.
sentences.zh: 它现在有点稳定。

sentences.en: Now it's in kind of a good place.
sentences.zh: 现在它处于一个挺不错的状态。

sentences.en: But there are changes I want to make.
sentences.zh: 但我还是有一些想做的改动。

sentences.en: And one of the things in particular is when I started, I really didn't realise the importance of this internal iteration that we were talking about.
sentences.zh: 其中特别的一点是，当我刚开始的时候，我真的没有意识到我们刚才讨论的这种内部迭代的重要性。

sentences.en: Because right now, it's purely an optimisation.
sentences.zh: 因为目前，它纯粹只是一种优化。

sentences.en: It's something that, if you are lucky, you know, if you know the library very well, then you know when you're going to hit this internal code, you know,
sentences.zh: 它是那种，如果你很幸运，你知道的，如果你对这个库非常熟悉，那么你就会知道什么时候会触及这个内部代码，你知道的，

sentences.en: internal iteration code path, and you know that that's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 内部迭代的代码路径，并且你知道这将会发生。

sentences.en: What I would like to do is to allow users to, like, be sure that they are going to be able to have this nice internal iteration happening.
sentences.zh: 我想要做的是，让用户能够确信他们一定能够实现这种优秀的内部迭代。

sentences.en: You know, to make that kind of a first class citizen of the Flux world, as it were.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，让它成为 Flux 世界中的一等公民，可以说是这样。

sentences.en: So at the moment, we have, and while I'm at it, really fixed the design around single pass sequences,
sentences.zh: 所以目前我们有，顺便说一句，真正修复了围绕单次遍历序列的设计，

sentences.en: because I have never been particularly happy about the way that that works in Flux.
sentences.zh: 因为我从来没有对 Flux 中这种机制的工作方式感到特别满意。

sentences.en: So the design at the moment that I've kind of been fleshing out in, like, notebooks and experiments over the past few months is to have a, whatever you want to call it,
sentences.zh: 因此，我过去几个月一直在笔记本和实验中不断完善的设计是，无论你想怎么称呼它，

sentences.en: an interface, a protocol, based purely around internal iteration.
sentences.zh: 一个纯粹基于内部迭代的接口、一个协议。

sentences.en: So we'll have a sequence is something on which you can call a function, let's call it iterate, that performs internal iteration, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们将有一个序列，你可以对其调用一个函数，我们暂且叫它 iterate，它执行内部迭代，对吧？

sentences.en: So you will call this iterate or iterate while, or whatever I end up calling it.
sentences.zh: 所以你将调用这个 iterate 或 iterate_while，或者我最终决定叫它什么的名字。

sentences.en: And you will pass it some predicates, and it will iterate through the sequence and call your predicate for each function and for each element until that predicate returns false,
sentences.zh: 然后你向它传递一些谓词，它将遍历序列并为每个函数和每个元素调用你的谓词，直到该谓词返回 false，

sentences.en: at which point iteration stops.
sentences.zh: 此时迭代停止。

sentences.en: Now, this is actually kind of weaker than the input iterators that we have in C++ at the moment,
sentences.zh: 现在，这实际上比我们目前在 C++ 中拥有的输入迭代器要弱一些，

sentences.en: because it's unspecified in this model what happens if you try to restart iteration after, you know, if your predicate returns false, we stop iterating.
sentences.zh: 因为在这个模型中，如果你试图在谓词返回 false 之后重新开始迭代，会发生什么是不确定的。

sentences.en: And then it's unspecified in this model what happens if you try to restart iteration, because if you think about it, if you're doing this over something like a vector,
sentences.zh: 然后在这个模型中，如果你试图重新开始迭代会发生什么也是不确定的，因为如果你仔细想想，如果你在像向量这样的对象上这样做，

sentences.en: the natural thing to do would be to restart iteration from the beginning again.
sentences.zh: 很自然的做法是从头开始重新迭代。

sentences.en: Whereas if you're using something like a stream, like a C++ input stream, then it's natural to just pick up from where you left off.
sentences.zh: 而如果你使用的是某种流，比如 C++ 输入流，那么很自然的做法就是从你刚才离开的地方继续。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so for this new kind of basic sequence API that's based around internal iteration, it's going to be unspecified what happens.
sentences.zh: 所以对于这种基于内部迭代的新型基础序列 API，发生什么将是不确定的。

sentences.en: So really, you need to only write algorithms that just stop somewhere, and then they are complete, which is fine.
sentences.zh: 因此实际上，你只需要编写那些在某个地方停下来就结束的算法，这没问题。

sentences.en: We can do that.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: But it means that the algorithms that you write using this protocol are slightly more limited than what you can write today with input iterators in C++ or with the single-pass model as it currently exists in Flux.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着用这个协议编写的算法，会比你今天在 C++ 中使用输入迭代器或使用 Flux 当前存在的单次遍历模型所能编写的算法稍微受限一些。

sentences.en: So that's kind of one end of the scale.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是天平的一端。

sentences.en: And then the other thing that I want to do is to have the current cursor model.
sentences.zh: 然后另一件我想做的事情是保留当前的游标模型。

sentences.en: Keep that, but only for multi-pass sequences.
sentences.zh: 保留它，但仅用于多次遍历序列。

sentences.en: So the current model that we have is that the operations of increment and dereference, that is access, these are separate operations.
sentences.zh: 所以我们目前的模型是，自增和解引用（也就是访问）的操作是独立的操纵。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So this is the same as with C++ iterators.
sentences.zh: 所以这与 C++ 迭代器是相同的。

sentences.en: And that works really, really well for multi-pass sequences.
sentences.zh: 这对于多次遍历序列来说效果真的非常非常好。

sentences.en: That is where we can repeatedly get the same element, get the same element out.
sentences.zh: 也就是说我们可以重复获取相同的元素，取出相同的元素。

sentences.en: Forward iterators.
sentences.zh: 前向迭代器。

sentences.en: Because these have a notion of position, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这些具有位置的概念，对吧？

sentences.en: That's kind of fundamentally multi-pass sequences.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是多次遍历序列的本质。

sentences.en: They have some idea of position.
sentences.zh: 它们有一些关于位置的概念。

sentences.en: We can have the cursor, as we call it, corresponds to a position.
